impl:sim-seams.summary:
I finished all eight sim-seams items: six fixed with tests, two (bounds and parts of the save table) investigated and handed to their owners with reproductions. The report is /home/user/foundress/docs/design/tasks/sim-seams-report.md.

1. Milestones and codex: a table test checks that every milestone, codex entry and aim has a trigger whose event some module really emits. It found that nothing emitted `world.zone-first-entry` or `world.micro-discovered`, so `ms-zone-crossed`, `ms-micro-connection`, `aim-cross-zone` and the habitat and joint codex entries could never fire. I added a stand-in emitter, `progression/discovery.ts`, and hooked the never-used `rival-discovered` event into `cx-formica` / `cx-pavement-wars`.
2. Journal: the winter jump moves the calendar start but not the tick, so every older entry was dated wrong, and after the jump no spring event fires. Entries now store the calendar tick they were written at (`calTick`), and the spring return gets its own entry.
3. Rivals at tick 1: almost all of the cost is inside nest-module carving, where one call takes 100-400 ms, so spreading it over ticks could not get under 50 ms. The rival nests are now built when the game is created (`rivals/prepare.ts`). The worst rivals tick went from 1475-1956 ms to under 4 ms on three archetypes, and new-game creation takes 1.7-2.4 s longer. The 2-game-day state hash changes because entity ids are handed out in a different order; the first differences are only shifted ids. With `rivals: 0` (R23) there are still no rivals and no foundations.
4. Commands: the system order was wrong, not the test. `nest-flood` and the phorid deaths ran after the end-of-tick corpse pass, so drowned ants vanished without a corpse and brood they carried stayed attached to a removed ant. Fixed in `systems.ts`; one test was out of date and is rewritten.
5. `time.auto-slow`: the event is not dead. The game layer owns the trigger and already emits it into the sim's event bus. I documented this on the type and added a test; the app needs to do nothing for the event.
6. Difficulty: the opening grace (`openingGraceGd`) is now wired: no scheduled human events, ant predators or bird visits during the first 0.3 game days of a played opening. That is two small logged cross-edits. The other unwired values stay flagged, each with the missing piece named. `autoSlowDefault` is left off the unwired list because the app is wiring it right now (uncommitted).
7. Bounds: no entity sat within 2 BU of the map limit after 2 game days, in five runs on three archetypes. No fix was needed.
8. Saves: dig, mid-time-lapse, hand-over, mid-human-event, mid-flood, the winter prompt and the first tick of spring all round-trip equal for 0.2 game days. Two cases differ, neither in my files: a rival colony's mound heights drift slightly after a load, and a save taken while paused, right after a command, loses that command's queued events.

findings.title: Zone-crossing milestone fires for the queen during the opening, not for a worker
findings.detail:
GDD 06 (§8 milestone table) defines ms-zone-crossed as 'a worker first enters a zone type other than the nest zone' ('A forager has crossed from {zone_from} onto {zone_to}'). The new stand-in emitter counts every ant of the player colony outside a nest, and the rule only checks isPlayerAntId.

In a real opening, createNewGame makes the founding nest record at the queen's landing point at tick 0. The foundress then walks the surface with nestId -1, usually possessed by the player. If her search crosses a zone edge, ms-zone-crossed completes during the founding with the forager text. The zone is marked seen, so no worker can trigger it later. aim-cross-zone opens at stage 'growing' and is never opened when already done, so that continuing aim is lost too.

Repro: src/sim/progression/discovery.verify.test.ts 'the queen walking into another zone is not "a worker" crossing' fails: the milestone is recorded at tick 4 by the queen.

Fix in the owned path: count only workers (caste !== 'queen'/'male'), or keep separate seen-bits for workers. The codex habitat entries can stay per colony.

findings.title: createNewGame now throws unless rivals/wiring.ts has been loaded
findings.detail:
Before this change initRivals only used entity helpers. Now it calls the late-bound rivalsImpl(), which is only provided once ants/behaviours/outdoor/index.ts, and through it rivals/wiring.ts, is in the import graph (normally via sim.ts / systems.ts).

A module or tool that imports only @/sim/createGame and creates a game on a world with rival sites now throws 'rivals: src/sim/rivals/wiring.ts was not loaded'. Repro: node tools/sim/run-ts.mjs test-output/sim-seams-review/lateBind.ts.

No caller is affected today: every current createNewGame caller also imports sim or testing. It is a hidden import-order trap, the same kind as the ecology cycle the report describes. Either import './wiring' from prepare's entry (if the cycle allows), or fall back to the first-tick path when no implementation is provided.

findings.title: Per-species-module stagger tests check nothing
findings.detail:
'<module>: every collision in a game of that species involves one of its own systems' passes for any collision that involves one of the module's own systems. Every collision that does not is a core-against-core collision, which the core test already asserts is empty.

So these tests can never fail, and any new collision between a species system and a core system (or within the module) is now accepted silently. The original guard 'no two periodic systems of 50+ ticks on one tick' is effectively removed for species modules.

Better: keep an explicit allowlist of today's known collisions (granary, fungus and wood counts from test-output/sim-seams/stagger.txt) and fail on anything new.

findings.detail:
The spec asks for each founding phase and mid-hunt. The report lists seal and lay as 'not reached' and mid-hunt as 'not measured'. Both phases can be reached cheaply with colony/founding/sealKit.ts throatCase.

fix:sim-seams.summary:
I reproduced all four review findings. The three code findings were real and are fixed with tests; the fourth was a test gap that the reviewer's own new test closes. Typecheck is clean. Every test in my folders passes except one test in time.test.ts, which fails because of another module's line.

(1) Major, the zone milestone fired for the queen. The stand-in emitter counted every ant of the colony, and the rule only checked the colony. The world event `world.zone-first-entry` keeps its meaning: the colony's first entry into a zone type, so the habitat codex entries still unlock from the queen's search. `ms-zone-crossed` now needs a worker caste, as GDD 06 §8 says ("a worker first enters"). The zone may already have had its first-entry event from the queen, so discovery.ts saves the first worker crossing out of the nest zone in trigger memory (`zoneCrossedTo`, saved with the state). The rule fires from that memory on the poll, and the event path stays for a worker's own first entry. No second first-entry event is sent. The reviewer's test that was red on purpose is now green.

(2) Minor, createNewGame threw unless rivals/wiring.ts was loaded. Reproduced with test-output/sim-seams-fix/createOnly.ts: it printed THROWS before the fix and creates the game after. initRivals now takes the heavy half only if it is loaded (`rivalsImplIfLoaded()`); otherwise the first rivals tick builds the nests, the same path older saves use. I did not import wiring.ts from the rivals index, because the index has to stay light: combat imports it, and an import loop there might only break in the browser build.

(3) Minor, the per-species stagger tests could never fail. They are replaced by an exact list of the system pairs that collide today (`KNOWN_PAIRS`: wood 7, granary 11, fungus 11, honeydew 0). Any other pair fails, and a self-check proves a new collision with a core system is caught.

(4) The reviewer's foundingPhases.verify.test.ts passes. It now covers the seal and lay rows of the item 8 table in the report.
